thread:
maria: Heads up — since 03:20 UTC we're seeing a capacity-signal drift for hosted-euw2-gpu. Admission control reports far fewer available slots than expected, queueing spike on small gen workloads. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/euw2/capacity

infra-bot: Alert: gpu-pool-euw2: AdmissionCapacityDrop (15m) severity=warning · runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/admission-drop

jonathan: What metrics are drifting specifically?

maria: p95 queue latency jumped to ~2.6s, admission headroom went 120 -> 42 over ~12m, token throughput steady. No mass evictions yet but admission rejects increased ~3x.

priya: Could be autoscaler misreporting allocatable. Any kube events or node conditions?

eli: quick check — ran `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-euw2 -o wide` and `kubectl describe nodes` on a few. NotReady=0, but kubelet reports reduced allocatable GPUs on 3 hosts (allocatable.gpu: 0 instead of 8). Suspect device-plugin or node-exporter hiccup.

maria: I also pulled `kubectl top nodes` — three hosts showing 40% less allocatable memory than baseline. CPU fine. GPU device plugin logs show intermittent registration timeouts. snippet:
```
2026-03-18T03:21:04Z device-plugin: registration timeout, retrying
2026-03-18T03:22:11Z device-plugin: registered 0 devices
```

samir: Sounds like a device-plugin flake. We should avoid draining whole AZ. Proposal: temporary routing weight shift (delta-router) to route ~20% of traffic away from euw2 while we patch the plugin + restart kubelets. Also drop low-priority batch pods first via adaptive eviction. PR for eviction helper: https://github.com/redwood/infralib/pull/482

jonathan: Risk? rollback plan?

priya: Minimal risk if we only tweak weights and restart the device-plugin service on affected nodes. If routing change needed, can revert in <5m. For the kubelet restart we can canary 1 node in az-a, observe admission capacity and p95 for 10m.

eli: I'm going to restart `kubelet` and `nvidia-device-plugin` on n3a-euw2-07 in 10m and post logs. Will not drain. :eyes:

maria: Plan of action: 1) Reduce delta-router weight to shift ~20% to us-west (samir to apply) 2) Canaried restart device-plugin + kubelet on n3a-euw2-07 (eli) 3) Deploy device-plugin restart helper (infra lib PR) if canary looks good 4) Monitor admission_headroom, p95 queue, and admissions rejects for 10m windows — rollback routing if no improvement.

samir: I'll open the routing change now and tag the deploy: `infra-router/changes/1954321000`. Will post PR link.

infra-bot: Incident note created IF-2026-123 · severity=warning · owner=eng-infra · linked-alert=gpu-pool-euw2.AdmissionCapacityDrop

jonathan: If canary succeeds, we should add a short-term alert to detect device-plugin restarts per node (threshold 3/10m) to catch recurrence.

maria: Agreed. I'll add that alert and add the device-plugin metric to the admission SLO dashboard. Updating ticket with runbook steps.

eli: Restart done on n3a-euw2-07 — device-plugin re-registered, allocatable.gpu back to 8. Posting logs and metrics snapshot in ticket. p95 dropped to 1.1s on that canary shard.

maria: Nice. Samir — please keep routing change for 20m then start rolling helper. We'll meet in #incident-ops if p95 flaps.

samir: Roger. I've applied the weight shift and will monitor. :thumbsup:

maria: On it. Will update here in 15m with roll status and metric diffs.
